$comment: Every one of the eleven closed constraint keywords at its boundary and one past it. Each expectation is read off the keyword table in `### Constraint keywords` of `spec/functional/FR-066-generate-runtime-validators.md` together with the operand the named constraint declares in `ir/constraints.ir.json`; the expected code is that constraint's own `diagnosticCode`, which FR-066 requires the validator to report rather than minting one. None was recorded from a run.

cases.title: minLength 2: a two-code-point string is at the bound and accepted
minLength 2: a one-code-point string is one past the bound
minLength counts code points, so one astral character counts once and fails a bound of two
minLength counts code points: one astral character and one ASCII make two
maxLength 4: a four-code-point string is at the bound and accepted
maxLength 4: a five-code-point string is one past the bound
an unanchored pattern matches an embedded substring, proving no anchor was added
an unanchored pattern still rejects a string it does not occur in
an anchored pattern matches only the whole string
an anchored pattern rejects the embedded form the unanchored one accepts
enumValues: a declared member is accepted
enumValues: a value outside the declared set is rejected
nonEmpty: one character is at the bound and accepted
nonEmpty: the empty string is one past the bound
format: a value satisfying the declared format is accepted
format: a value that is not of the declared format is rejected
min 0: zero is at the bound and accepted
min 0: minus one is one past the bound
max 10: ten is at the bound and accepted
max 10: eleven is one past the bound
exclusiveMin 0: a value above the bound is accepted
exclusiveMin 0: the bound itself is excluded
exclusiveMax 10: a value below the bound is accepted
exclusiveMax 10: the bound itself is excluded
maxLength 3 on a bytes subject: four base64 characters decoding to three octets are at the bound
cases.differentialReason: JSON Schema 2020-12 states `contentEncoding` as an annotation and ajv does not decode it, so the second decider counts base64 characters where FR-066 counts decoded octets. Teaching the schema the octet rule would be authoring the answer rather than a second reading.

cases.title: maxLength 3 on a bytes subject: eight base64 characters decoding to four octets are one past it
cases.differentialReason: As CONS-025: the decoded-octet length is outside the JSON data model ajv validates in.

cases.title: a bytes subject rejects a string that is not well-formed base64
cases.differentialReason: The base64 well-formedness rule is a declared backend decision pending agent-ix/filament-core-data#58, not a published contract clause, so a hand-authored schema asserting it would restate the decision rather than check it.

cases.title: unique: two distinct members are accepted
unique: two members sharing a canonical form are rejected
a constrained scalar validated directly reports at the root pointer
a constrained scalar at its bound is accepted when validated directly
